preconditions.expression: all(0 <= d_i <= n for d_i in d) and 0 in d and n in d and len(d) == m and m >= 2 and n >= 1 and m <= min(n + 1, 10**4) and g >= 1 and r >= 1 and g <= 1000 and r <= 1000
preconditions.description: Input consists of integers n (road width), m (number of safety islands), distinct safety island coordinates d_1, ..., d_m (including 0 and n), and traffic light timings g (green) and r (red). All values are within specified bounds.
All safety island coordinates are distinct.

postconditions.description: Output is either -1 (impossible) or a non-negative integer representing the minimal time to cross the road.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (all(0 <= pos <= n for pos in path) and path[0] == 0 and path[-1] == n and len(path) == int(stdout) + 1 and all(abs(path[i+1] - path[i]) == 1 for i in range(len(path)-1)))
postconditions.description: If output is not -1, there exists a valid path (sequence of positions) of length equal to the output time + 1, starting at 0, ending at n, and moving exactly ±1 per second while staying within [0, n].

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (all((time % (g + r) < g) or (pos in d) for time, pos in enumerate(path)) and all((time % (g + r) >= g) == (pos in d) for time, pos in enumerate(path)))
postconditions.description: If output is not -1, Denis is on a safety island whenever the light is red (time % (g + r) >= g), and can be anywhere during green light (time % (g + r) < g).

postconditions.expression: stdout == '-1' or (all((path[i+1] - path[i] == -1 and (path[i] in d or path[i+1] in d)) or (path[i+1] - path[i] == 1 and (path[i] in d or path[i+1] in d)) or (path[i+1] - path[i] == -1 and path[i] not in d and path[i+1] not in d and (path[i-1] - path[i] == -1 if i > 0 else True)) or (path[i+1] - path[i] == 1 and path[i] not in d and path[i+1] not in d and (path[i-1] - path[i] == 1 if i > 0 else True)) for i in range(len(path)-1)))
postconditions.description: If output is not -1, Denis can only change direction (±1) on safety islands. Otherwise, he must continue in the same direction (±1) unless forced by boundaries.
If output is not -1, it is the minimal possible time to cross the road under the given constraints.
